title: Settings file — software-analysis capability
description: Formal shape of the project's `.pkit/capabilities/software-analysis/project/config.yaml`: the settings of the capability a project chooses. The capability's README describes each setting, in its section "Configuration". This schema checks the shape only. The stamp (`pkit analysis new`) and the number check (`pkit analysis check-numbers`) ask git whether each entry holds. Document-shaped schema: the file IS the resource (no top-level id collection). Companion per COR-018.

binds_to.description: Repo-relative globs matching the adopter-data files this schema validates (COR-023 fallback binding). Present on the capability-side carrier; absent from a project's file.

analyses.description: The analyses the project keeps, one for each component that keeps one (DEC-001 point 2). Absent, or empty, where it keeps one, at the top of the analysis location. Listed, each lies in a folder of the location named after its component, and an artefact no listed analysis holds is refused. One numbering of each numbered kind runs across them, and no two of their artefacts share an id (DEC-001 point 3).

numbering.description: How use cases, journeys and requirements are numbered (DEC-001 point 3, DEC-002 point 2).

freed-by.description: Ids a person declares free again, declaring that nothing cites them: a pilot abandoned before anything cited it, say. Each entry names the commit that removed the artefacts and lists their ids. The stamp gives a listed id again, and the number check does not count it as taken. The README's section "Configuration" says what cites an id and which ids a commit can free.

analysis.description: One analysis: its component, the folder of the analysis location it lies in, and the analyses it builds on.

component.description: The component it describes, a part of the system developed and versioned on its own, by its name. `core` names a methodology's core, the backbone; a capability goes by its own name.

folder.description: The folder of the analysis location it lies in, one word, named after its component.

builds-on.description: The analyses it builds on: those of the components its component depends on, required or optional, and no other (DEC-001 point 2; RS-SAN-010). Where the component declares its dependencies, as a capability does in its package metadata, validation holds this list to them.

analysis.description: The analysis it builds on, by its component's name.

optional.description: Whether its component is an optional dependency: used only where present, and the analysis works without it. False unless set.

entry.description: One commit and the ids it frees.

ids.description: The use cases, journeys and requirements the commit removed whose ids are free again. Only a listed id is freed.

commit-id.description: A commit, by its full hexadecimal id in lower case — 40 digits, or 64 in a SHA-256 repository: an abbreviation can come to name two commits as history grows. Quoted in YAML, as digits alone can read as a number.
